name: Flat Vector Illustration
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not a verified style label from the source collection. Use simplified figures, flat color fields, consistent corner radii, and proportionate icons, outlines, and type. Communicate with masks, decomposition, and meaningful shape changes; hold key text. Avoid photorealistic reflections, complex materials, and inconsistent shadows. SVG alone does not establish the look.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to explainers, brand pieces, mascots, product stories, and illustrated narratives. It can support video or interactive HTML. Interactive examples include keyboard-navigable product tours and responsive SVG charts with accessible tables and focusable data points. These are recommendations, not verified uses in a source video.
limitations: Keep illustrations legible and uncluttered. Chart morphs must preserve meaning; use honest scales and do not invent data. Suggested data scenes limit series to three. Omit gaze-following when eyes or rigs are unsuitable or movement distorts the face. Chapter handoffs can obscure causality, violate continuous-shot or loop requirements, or add needless structure. No source-video verification or fixed production toolchain is claimed.
palette: Visual guidance calls for three to five main colors and a fixed accent. Optional new-art palette: five discrete flat tokens—background #F7F3E9, foreground #243746, accent_1 #267D82, coral accent_2 #DD7353, accent_3 #EAC664. These are suggestions, not canonical colors; exact task, brand, approved, semantic, and asset colors take precedence. Preserve roles and families; no gradients or extra hues. Contrast examples: foreground/background 11.083:1; foreground on accent_3 7.462:1; text on accent_1 or accent_2 fails the 4.5:1 normal-text target. Recheck composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Use staged entrances, eased masks, path motion, decomposition, and semantically clear morphs; preserve holds, deliberate cuts, impacts, and constant-speed sections. For HTML, chapter/story states may scrub with finite scroll progress and reverse coherently; provide reading order and reduced-motion/static states. Pointer gaze is optional, bounded to eye sockets, and returns to neutral. Video must derive all state from seekable composition time, independent of live input; direct and backward seeks should match playback.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory layer. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and user requirements; leave room for reading and speech. Use authorized assets, synchronize and mix with picture, and check intelligibility, balance, clipping, and sync.
assetRequirements: Build flat artwork from SVG primitives and groups; use suitable layered character assets or a rig for facial motion. Load fonts and assets before animation. Optional PixiJS can render layered 2D sprites and masks; tldraw can author editable diagram assets but is not a renderer. Preserve contours and palette. Verify geometry, labels, crop, scale, and missing assets.
combinations: Usually works alone. With style-095, place animated UI inside flat device frames, matching radii and palette, without glass, realistic shadows, new UI colors, or busy micro-motion; coral is the CTA accent. With style-097, morph illustrated objects into accurately scaled flat charts, use primary tokens, readable labels, and no gradients, 3D bars, invented data, or more than three series.
productionApproach: Choose visual renderer and motion engine by style, action, assets, and fidelity; use one owner per animated property. SVG is the direct drawing route; GSAP is the primary seekable motion layer. Optional tools include Motion, Anime.js, mo.js, Paper.js, and PixiJS when their specific capability fits and seeking is verified. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required output, and record why. The pipeline does not own the style rendering. Inspect key frames and decoded output; provide editable source, contact sheet, parameters, and reproducible render instructions.
